# ui::ButtonVisual

Header: `winui/ui/themes/Theme.hpp`.

How a button-shaped surface looks in one interaction state: its fill, border and label color, plus the optional era layers (bevels, gradients, inner rings, wells) that [`draw_control_chrome`](../rendering/namespace-ui.md#draw_control_chrome) draws.

[Theme](theme.md) holds one per state per style (`button_normal`, `accent_button_hover`, ...), and the built-in toggles, sliders and swipe items use the same type. A plain `ButtonVisual{background, border, text}` leaves every optional layer off and draws a flat rounded surface. The other fields are for themes that reproduce an era.

Example: 
```cpp
ui::Theme theme = ui::Theme::light();
theme.button_hover = ui::ButtonVisual{ui::Color::from_argb(0xFFE0E0E0), // background
                                         ui::Color::from_argb(0xFF808080), // border
                                         ui::colors::Black};               // label
theme.button_hover.border_width = 2.0f; // this state only; the rest keep Theme::border_width
window.pin_theme(std::move(theme));
```

## background

```cpp
Color background
```

The flat fill. Also set as the fallback color when [`background_gradient`](#background_gradient) is set.

## border

```cpp
Color border
```

The outline color, for a surface that draws a flat border.

## text

```cpp
Color text
```

The label, glyph or mark drawn on the surface.

## border_style

```cpp
BorderStyle border_style = BorderStyle::Rounded
```

For era themes only. Every field below defaults to off, so an aggregate-initialized ButtonVisual{bg, border, text} draws a plain flat surface.

Flat and Rounded, the default, draw no separate border, and [`background`](#background) is the whole fill. Raised and Sunken draw a classic 3-D edge around the fill with render/Bevel.hpp's [draw_bevel_border()](../rendering/namespace-ui.md#draw_bevel_border), from the `bevel_*` colors below, in place of the border and gradient fields.

## bevel_light

```cpp
Color bevel_light = colors::White
```

The four bevel rings. [`bevel_light`](#bevel_light) is the outer top/left ring, [`bevel_highlight`](#bevel_highlight) the inner top/left ring, [`bevel_shadow`](#bevel_shadow) the inner bottom/right ring and [`bevel_dark_shadow`](#bevel_dark_shadow) the outer bottom/right ring, the hard dark edge at a raised button's bottom-right corner. Windows 95 and 98 use five distinct colors with the face: `#FFFFFF`, `#DFDFDF`, `#C0C0C0`, `#808080` and `#000000`. Windows 2000 makes the light ring the face color and softens the dark ring to `#404040`, so the same edge has visibly lower contrast.

## bevel_highlight

```cpp
Color bevel_highlight = colors::White
```

## bevel_shadow

```cpp
Color bevel_shadow = Color::from_argb(0xFF808080)
```

## bevel_dark_shadow

```cpp
Color bevel_dark_shadow = colors::Black
```

## bevel_soft

```cpp
bool bevel_soft = false
```

The push-button arrangement, which swaps the two top/left rings (render/Bevel.hpp). Set only on push-button visuals. A window border, field well or check-box well keeps the plain arrangement, since the era draws both.

## bevel_rings

```cpp
int bevel_rings = 2
```

How many of the two bevel rings to draw. The era's hot toolbar button is a single edge with no second ring, a third raised shape next to the window border and the push button (render/Bevel.hpp's `rings`).

## bevel_frame

```cpp
std::optional<Color> bevel_frame {}
```

Windows 3.x only. When set, the edge is drawn by [`draw_win3x_border`](../rendering/namespace-ui.md#draw_win3x_border) instead of [`draw_bevel_border`](../rendering/namespace-ui.md#draw_bevel_border): a 1px frame in this color on all four sides, with a 1px [`bevel_highlight`](#bevel_highlight) on the top and left and a 2px [`bevel_shadow`](#bevel_shadow) on the right and bottom inside it. The pressed state drops the bottom and right edge entirely. [`bevel_light`](#bevel_light) and [`bevel_dark_shadow`](#bevel_dark_shadow) are not used here, since Windows 3.x has no outer bevel rings. Unset everywhere else.

## background_gradient

```cpp
std::optional<LinearGradientBrush> background_gradient {}
```

A top-to-bottom gradient fill in place of [`background`](#background), for Luna and Aero. [`background`](#background) stays set alongside it as a flat fallback for code that only needs the button's rough color.

## inner_border

```cpp
std::optional<LinearGradientBrush> inner_border {}
```

Aero's inner highlight ring, the fourth layer of its button: a second 1px stroke one pixel inside the outer border, with a radius one less. The outer border sits at `(0.5, 0.5, w-1, h-1)` with radius 2.75 and this ring at `(1.5, 1.5, w-3, h-3)` with radius 1.75. It makes an Aero surface look like a lit bevel, and its color marks three states: white `#FAFFFFFF` to `#85FFFFFF` at rest and disabled, absent when pressed (the press animation fades it out first), and solid cyan `#F900CCFF` on the default button, the era's only default-button cue. The gradient stretches over the ring's own height, where [`border_gradient`](#border_gradient) below spans a fixed number of pixels.

## inner_border_width

```cpp
float inner_border_width = 1.0f
```

How thick that ring is. Aero's is one pixel, the default. Luna's is two: the amber glow of a hot button sits 2 px thick inside its 1px `#003C74` border, and the check box's ring is 2 px too, inset by 1 px. A 1px ring would look like a thin outline instead of a glow.

## inner_shadow

```cpp
std::optional<Color> inner_shadow {}
```

Aero's pressed inner shadow: two 2px bands inside the top and left edges, fading from this color to transparent, drawn over the fill and under the border. Aero shows a press by shading the button's inside, and the label stays where it is.

## inset_well

```cpp
std::optional<InsetWell> inset_well {}
```

Aero's check box and radio button only (see [`InsetWell`](inset-well.md)): the rim and fill drawn inside the well, over [`background`](#background) and under the border. Unset everywhere else.

## border_gradient

```cpp
std::optional<LinearGradientBrush> border_gradient {}
```

Fluent's elevation border: a gradient stroke drawn in place of a flat [`border`](#border) when set, which makes the control look slightly raised. [Theme::fluent()](theme.md#fluent) sets it only on the neutral and accent buttons at rest and on hover. Every other ButtonVisual leaves it unset: pressed and disabled states, subtle buttons, toggle indicators, and the era and high-contrast themes. The gradient spans [`border_gradient_extent_px`](#border_gradient_extent_px) device pixels whatever the control's height. A positive span starts at the top edge, and a negative one starts at the bottom edge with the stops reversed (see [StrokeRoundedRectGradient](../rendering/render-commands.md#struct-strokeroundedrectgradient)).

## border_gradient_extent_px

```cpp
float border_gradient_extent_px = 3.0f
```

## mark_border_gradient

```cpp
std::optional<LinearGradientBrush> mark_border_gradient {}
```

The same raised look on the mark drawn over the indicator. The gradient runs from top to bottom over the mark's own height, with [`Palette::control_stroke_default`](palette.md#control_stroke_default) at 50 % and [`Palette::control_stroke_secondary`](palette.md#control_stroke_secondary) at 70 %, in light and dark alike. Unlike [`border_gradient`](#border_gradient) it stretches with the mark: the upper half is the faint color and the lower 30 % the stronger one, whatever the mark's size. It is stroked 1 pixel inside the mark. Only [RadioButton](../controls/radio-button.md#uiradiobutton) reads it, for its dot, and only [`Theme::fluent()`](theme.md#fluent)'s checked ring sets it.

## mark_gradient

```cpp
std::optional<RadialGradientBrush> mark_gradient {}
```

Aero's radio dot: a radial fill lit from the top left and sized to the dot, with a flat [`mark_stroke`](#mark_stroke) ring 1px inside its edge, in place of the flat [`text`](#text) disc. [RadioButton](../controls/radio-button.md#uiradiobutton) only, and only where set. When it is set on an unchecked state the dot is drawn anyway, which is how the era previews a press. The gradient dot is drawn in render() only, and never animated as a one-color layer.

## mark_stroke

```cpp
std::optional<Color> mark_stroke {}
```

## text_effect

```cpp
TextEffect text_effect {}
```

The classic engraved look of a disabled label (see [TextEffect](../rendering/text-effect.md)). The default draws the label once, in plain color.

## border_width

```cpp
OptionalFloat border_width {}
```

This visual's own border width, for themes such as Windows 8.1, whose dark mode has a 2px [Button](../controls/button.md#uibutton) outline and a 0px [CheckBox](../controls/check-box.md#uicheckbox) outline, and light mode the opposite. Unset, the default, uses [`Theme::border_width`](theme.md#border_width) (see [resolved_border_width()](#resolved_border_width)).

## draw_border

```cpp
bool draw_border = false
```

Draws a flat stroke in [`border`](#border) at the resolved width even when the caller of [draw_control_chrome()](../rendering/namespace-ui.md#draw_control_chrome) did not ask for one through `draw_flat_border_fallback`. Metro's dark [Button](../controls/button.md#uibutton) is only this stroke, a 2px outline with no fill. Defaults to false.

## resolved_border_width

```cpp
float resolved_border_width(float theme_default) const
```

Returns this visual's [`border_width`](#border_width) if it set one, otherwise `theme_default`, which is [`Theme::border_width`](theme.md#border_width). A control that draws its border itself, without [draw_control_chrome()](../rendering/namespace-ui.md#draw_control_chrome), calls this to get the same width [draw_control_chrome()](../rendering/namespace-ui.md#draw_control_chrome) would use.
